text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Potentially violent showdowns loom in the city and elsewhere in the country as reformists say they will go ahead with pro-reform rallies planned for Monday.
- Top criminal suspect Bernard Matheri Thuo alias Rasta, who has a 100,000 shillings reward on his head, slips through a police dragnet and survives a day-long operation to track him down.
- The head of the Roman Catholic Church in Kenya urges both the government and the opposition to avoid violent clashes during Monday's unlicensed rallies.
- A German preacher and four streetchildren are among at least 200 people arrested by police in Eldoret town, Rift Valley, in a crackdown on suspected reform activists.
- The Executive Council of the National Convention Assembly asks Kenyans to choose between attending today's pro-reform meetings, staying at home or going to work.
- The Zambian government withdraws provisional flight facilities for Kenya Airways in Zambia following misunderstandings between Kenya Airways and Aero-Zambia.
- The ruling party, the Kenya African National Union, rejects demands for dialogue by the opposition.
- President Daniel arap Moi is scheduled to chair the sixth assembly of the Inter-Governmental Authority on Development (IGAD) in Nairobi on Tuesday.
- President Moi says some foreigners are colluding with the opposition to destabilise the country.
- The International Monetary Fund blocks a $37 million loan to Kenya because of the High Court's decision to terminate the 5.8 billion shillings Goldenberg scam court case.

- A tense 90-minute meeting at State House Nairobi between President Moi and eight senior diplomats has convinced donor countries that the government will not hold talks with the opposition about constitutional reforms before the general election.
- The Organisation of African Unity is working to find a common position on the United States initiative for an African peace-keeping force.
